analysis.title: Three Clearing Events To Capitulation: Morgan Stanley's Wilson Says The Correction Isn't Done Yet
key_insights: Morgan Stanley's Mike Wilson says the correction that began in June is in its final stages, with much of the damage done beneath the surface, but three clearing events remain and may need to worsen conditions before they improve.

Tactical downside target for the S&P 500 is 7100-7200, a slight break of the 200-day moving average. With the S&P at 7,624 when the note went out, that is a drop of roughly 6-7%. Year-end base case remains 8000, and the 12-month base case is 8,300.

Roughly 60% of Russell 3000 stocks are down more than 20% from highs since June 1, more than a third are down 30%, and one in eight is down more than 50%. 96% of chip stocks are down 20%+, 87% are down 30%+, and 42% are down 50%+. Software is 77% down 20%+, Tech Hardware 72%, and only 7% of Banks.

Wilson sees a mid-cycle transition: early-cycle, high-leverage stocks (semis, autos, consumer, media, financials) are hit while investors crowd into quality. He expects the index to converge with weaker breadth, meeting in the middle. Breadth has started to improve from narrow levels.
Breadth improvement needs to come from actual buying rather than short covering as gross exposures are reduced. The recent bounce in the average stock was largely hedge funds covering shorts.

Clearing Event #1 is the AI funding glut: doubts about return on capital, the cost of capital for some AI players, and whether credit markets can fund the spending. More supply is expected over the next month, and credit spreads for lower-quality players may stay wider. Semis and capex beneficiaries are the epicenter.
Meta is raising up to $95 billion in equity, larger than Alphabet's $84.75 billion June raise, with its own chip suppliers buying in.

Morgan Stanley's charts point to semis support in mid-November, about 10-15% lower, with an A-B-C pattern targeting roughly 9,500 on the SOX. Wilson expects the low to coincide with funding concerns bottoming.

Retail bought the semis dip with 3x leverage in record size as semis fell 11% in a week, while hedge funds reversed all AI net buying since the start of 2025. Hedge fund positioning has come down substantially while retail and passive investors remain more fully invested.
3Q EPS surprise is running at 2%, less than half the 4.4% historical average, and the median stock's next-day reaction is 0.0%. 44.5% of S&P market cap reports this week.

2Q net income rose 53% y/y, with roughly half from non-operating profit such as unrealized gains on private AI investments. Excluding those, 2Q growth was 27%. The same gains create tough y/y comps for AI names into 2027.

Clearing Event #2 is the midterms next Tuesday. Since 1950 the S&P has been higher 6 and 12 months after every midterm, with average gains of 14.8% and 16.6%. A blue wave is consensus per polls and betting markets, and the bigger surprise would be a GOP Senate or a Democratic margin of 53-55+ seats.

The larger post-election overhang is the administration floating escalation of the war in Iran or other action after the vote. Wilson says such surprises have often led to excellent short-term buying opportunities and could cause the final capitulation.

Clearing Event #3 is Warsh's liquidity squeeze, which Wilson calls the biggest risk and catalyst for a final low. Warsh has hiked once and has slowed the growth of the Fed's balance sheet by about half. Morgan Stanley's composite of rates, the dollar and energy is on par with 2018 and almost as severe as 2022.

Wilson does not expect fireworks from Wednesday's FOMC since front- and back-end rates have repriced 30-40bps lower in recent weeks. Funding markets are calm (SOFR spreads and interbank rates not forcing intervention), so the Fed has no reason to act. Wilson is watching for early signs the Fed adds liquidity, as in 2018.

Treasury buybacks crushed bond vol in March and April. Bond vol has been stickier recently, the MOVE is well above the VIX, and Wilson thinks Treasury may need to increase buybacks. A sizable TGA balance could be deployed.

Wilson's comprehensive sentiment indicator is at a neutral level, not at capitulation extremes. He expects a reading near the lows seen earlier this year when the Iran war began before the correction ends.
Wilson continues to favor quality while remaining patient to add risk more aggressively. The author (ZeroHedge) argues the index may fall further and faster than 6-7%.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says the correction is in its final stages with the damage done beneath the surface, and expects a rally to 8000 by year-end.
tension_points.bear_case: Sentiment is still neutral, retail is buying semis with 3x leverage, and the index may fall further and faster than 6-7% (ZeroHedge view).
tension_points.what_invalidates: Sentiment reaching a capitulation reading near the earlier-year lows would mark the low; the Fed adding liquidity would signal the clearing event has passed.

tension_points.bull_case: Wilson says once the supply is cleared the risk should subside, and expects semis to bottom in mid-November alongside funding concerns.
tension_points.bear_case: Meta alone is raising up to $95B with its suppliers in the book, and credit spreads for lower-quality players may stay wider.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The SOX falling past about 9,500 in mid-November would break the mid-November low call.
